_about: Christine de Pisan. Bloom's Western Canon (1994) lists: The Book of the City of Ladies. Bloom addition 2026-11-03 under Adam's Bloom-only ruling. The text is the EEBO-TCP transcription of the 1521 Pepwell printing, keyed by hand from the page images (the scan's own OCR was black-letter garble). Spelling is 1521's; TCP marks every unread letter as a <gap>, never a guess.

pisan-boke-cyte-ladyes: The Boke of the Cyte of Ladyes

pisan-boke-cyte-ladyes.bloom_title: The Book of the City of Ladies
pisan-boke-cyte-ladyes.evidence: TCP catalogue A20897 read (Christine, de Pisan; Anslay, Brian; 1521; 382 pp.); file's <availability> states CC0 1.0; Anslay named in the book's own text.
pisan-boke-cyte-ladyes.case: Bloom lists the City of Ladies. Brian Anslay's 1521 English is the only pre-1931 translation, and the TCP transcription is a clean, hand-keyed witness of it.
pisan-boke-cyte-ladyes.note: The book's body never names Christine (the 1521 printing calls her by her work); the identity check passes on Anslay and the title. 203 illegible gaps marked by the keyers. Replaces the 2026-11-03 IA attempt (the-boke-of-the-cyte-of-ladyes), whose OCR failed the gate.
